fieldValues.title: The three lines and their poles
fieldValues.article_text:
The three lines and their poles are the core practice: every boundary and tension in our work is read by the same rules. This is the canonical statement; it is an evolving theory, refined by practice, not a truth.

The generative sequence (from the owner's T3 Foundations, greenmans_creation obsidian-vault/1-Systems-and-Topology/T3-Foundations.md):
- Wuji: undifferentiated potential; no boundary, no system.
- Taiji: the first boundary, inside and outside; a system appears. Nothing below can be read until the boundary is named.
- Liang Yi, the two primordials: line 1 appears, yang and yin.
- Si Xiang, the four images: line 2 divides each.
- Bagua, the eight images: line 3 completes the cube, 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 positions.

The three lines, read from the bottom (yin pole first, yang second):
1. Line 1, Earth (energy). Observe ↔ Act: gather information and refine ourselves, letting energy in to change the system itself; or act now and outward, applying energy onto the world. In T3: Input ↔ Output.
2. Line 2, Human (time). Stabilise ↔ Disrupt: simplify and refine what is already present, letting the system settle; or evolve and add new things, adding energy to change state. In T3: Equilibrate ↔ Activate.
3. Line 3, Heaven (space). Zoom out ↔ Focus: an open boundary, synchronising with the context and other actors, with many options, many of them external; or a closed boundary steered by a goal we chose, with few options, mostly internal. In T3: Distribute ↔ Concentrate.

The eight images are the corners of the cube, the eight archetypal stances: Initiator ☰ Heaven (Act, Disrupt, Focus); Challenger ☱ Lake (Act, Disrupt, Zoom out); Synthesizer ☲ Fire (Act, Stabilise, Focus); Builder ☳ Thunder (Act, Stabilise, Zoom out); Analyst ☴ Wind (Observe, Disrupt, Focus); Rebel ☵ Water (Observe, Disrupt, Zoom out); Steward ☶ Mountain (Observe, Stabilise, Focus); Watcher ☷ Earth (Observe, Stabilise, Zoom out). An archetype is a stance a person or group can inhabit, recognise and invite when the system needs it; it is a position, not a type.

The systems reading (cybernetics): the boundary makes the system; line 1 is the exchange across it, acting on the environment or sensing it; line 2 is the system's state over time, changing or holding steady; line 3 is where control sits, concentrated at the centre or distributed among the parts. Health is the capacity to move between positions, not a best corner (metabolic flexibility). Applied at every scale, the same reading recurs in every narrower boundary, as in Beer's viable system model.

The rules, the same everywhere:
1. Name the boundary first. A tension can be weighed only inside a domain; there is no polarity without one.
2. Every tension placed on a line is a trade-off: two goods, a coupled cost, a right position that moves with context (handbook, What a trade-off is).
3. Each pole has a shadow, the failure of leaning on it too hard: understeer and oversteer.
4. Yang is not good. Yang (Act, Disrupt, Focus) is thing over relation and outward over inward; preference is a separate lean, recorded on its own.
5. Polarity is assigned per domain and may flip in a narrower one (decision cdd272a3).
6. Fractal: a domain's tension on a line refines its parent's tension on the same line, back to these three.
7. A decision is a hypothesis placed on the lines: good enough for now, why, what would make us reconsider, and the shadows it might fall into.
8. Independence is tested with real cases: four for each pair (2×2), eight for all three (the cube).
fieldValues.rationale: The three lines already recur across the work (stances, domain axes, decision ratings, the archetypal flow, the older products model), two blind raters per line agreed at kappa 0.81 to 0.90 on 101 decisions, and the owner names them the core practice and the creation myth (vignettes 7007c3be, ffc72ab1).
fieldValues.amendment_rule: Refined by decision in a session, never by a quiet edit; each refinement keeps the earlier wording findable. The theory is expected to change as practice shows where it fails.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A line's reading stops being agreed by independent raters, trade-offs repeatedly fail to place on any line, or a fourth axis keeps appearing (the older model allowed a domain-specific wildcard). Open now: line 3 was described as 'not breadth: a small choice can be open, and a system-wide one closed' (the owner's Perspective tension) and, on 2026-10-25, as 'the scale of the boundary: a small set of mostly internal options, or a wide set, many external'. The two are not yet reconciled.
